Just as a note, I noticed `ansible-pull` accepts inventory options, but ignores everything other than `--inventory`. In another PR, we should either ensure `--limit`/`--list-host`/`--flush-cache` are not valid options for `ansible-pull`, or that they are passed through to `ansible-playbook` from `ansible-pull`, I'm not sure what makes the most sense.

Facts cache is not flushed.

**Test with --flush-cache:**

Facts cache is flushed.

Moved the `flush_cache` logic to CLI base class `_play_prereqs` method. Also, deleted the pattern from `playbook.py`.

Working on adding new tests for adhoc command.

Adding a test for `--flush-cache` in `test/integration/targets/adhoc` 

```
# --flush-cache option for ansible
# create facts_cache
rm -f localhost && ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN=jsonfile ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION=. ansible localhost -m setup > /dev/null && test -s localhost
# flush facts_cache
ansible --flush-cache localhost -m debug -a "msg={{ ansible_facts }}" | grep '"msg": {}'
```
Suggestions?

That looks good to me, just set the env vars in `test/integration/targets/adhoc/runme.sh` before the two tasks so the fact cache is also active for the test. Since ansible-test runs the tests in a tmp dir, there's no need to rm localhost.

```bash
# test ansible --flush-cache
export ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN=jsonfile
export ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION=./
# collect and cache facts
ansible localhost -m setup > /dev/null && test -s localhost
# test flushing the fact cache
ansible --flush-cache localhost -m debug -a "msg={{ ansible_facts }}" | grep '"msg": {}'
```

issue_context.title: Option to flush or ignore inventory cache for ad-hoc commands
issue_context.body:
### Summary

I would like an option like the ansible-playbook option `--flush-caches` for the `ansible` command.

I use the redis caching plugin to cache my (netbox) inventory. When I use ad-hoc commands to quickly test & perform one-off actions I would like the option to expire my cache immediately if I make changes to my inventory source(netbox) between runs.

At this moment the only thing that seems to work is to edit my inventory and set `cache:` to false there. Setting environment variables, or using `--extra-vars` doesn't seem to work. With `ansible-playbook` I currently use the `--flush-caches` option for this. That doesn't *disable* the cache, but just expires it, which has the same result for me.

### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

cli/adhoc

### Additional Information

-

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct
comments:

`ANSIBLE_INVENTORY_CACHE_CONNECTION="" ansible-playbook ...` but you just want it to be a switch? 

We are trying to avoid the proliferation of switches and recommend using the env or ansible vars.

@bcoca Well kind of;

Using `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY_CACHE_CONNECTION` exactly like you described doesn't seem to work (in my environment). It's like it doesn't overwrite my inventory config options at all.

Besides that, I'd like something that works with the `ansible` ad-hoc command. However I suspect that overriding my inventory file with an environment variable would work for that as well, if I got it working for ansible-playbook.

This is what my repository looks like:
### ansible-repo/ansible.cfg
```
[defaults]
inventory              = ./inventory/
...
```

### ansible-repo/inventory/netbox.yml
```
plugin: netbox.netbox.nb_inventory
...
cache: true
cache_plugin: community.general.redis
cache_timeout: 3600
cache_connection: "localhost:6379:0"
```

i was using 'one' option without knowing your exact context, if you set via a variable (which has higher precedence than env var) you need to 'unset' via  variable `-e cache_connection=""'`, if you are setting it in the inventory plugin itself, that has even higher precedence, so yes, you'll have to modify it there. But this is why we give many options on how to set things.   Even if we add a command line switch, the inventory direct setting would still have higher precedence.

`--flush-cache` seems like it could be moved from `add_meta_options` to `add_inventory_options`, since it's handled automatically in the CLI base class and used both as a CLI toggle for a meta task and is also passed to inventory plugins.

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/adhoc.py#L116 -> https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py#L563 -> https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/inventory/manager.py#L166 -> https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/inventory/manager.py#L227 -> https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/inventory/manager.py#L292

This should be easy to add since `--flush-cache` is passed directly to inventory plugins rather than a normal part of config. (Of course, it depends on the plugin, and if used as part of config, then it behaves as @bcoca describes.)
corrected, so easy fix is to add --flush-caches to ansible/ansible-console

Awesome!

And gathering from the [variable precedence list](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/playbook_guide/playbooks_variables.html#variable-precedence-where-should-i-put-a-variable) I thought `-e` should **always** take precedence, I didn't know inventory plugins configs took precedence over that. But editing the file is ok as a temporary solution, until this is gets implemented.

extra vars (-e) is the highest precedence among variables, in 'general precedence' variables have high precedence, but 'direct settings' to a plugin have the highest precedence. https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/reference_appendices/general_precedence.html , seems to be missing that last one, I'll update the documentation.

copying --flush-cache from add_meta_options to add_inventory_options and including the relevant flush_cache code from ansible-playbook into ansible-console seems to work.

i will test further...
